targets.authors: Vernon, P. A., Martin, R. A., Schermer, J. A., & Mackie, A.
targets.title: A behavioral genetic investigation of humor styles and their correlations with the Big Five personality dimensions.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of the present study was to attempt to replicate the Vernon et al. (in press) finding that individual differences in affiliative and self-enhancing humor were largely attributable to additive genetic and nonshared environmental factors, whereas individual differences in aggressive and self-defeating humor were largely attributable to shared and nonshared environmental factors.
targets.outcome_quote: In conclusion, our present study successfully replicated the Vernon et al. (in press) finding that individual differences in two positive styles of humor — affiliative and self-enhancing — are largely attributable to genetic and nonshared environmental factors. Unlike Vernon et al. (in press), however, our present study found little evidence for an influence of shared environmental factors on individual differences in negative styles of humor.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm the two positive humor findings and explicitly contrast the two negative humor findings. Their confirmation is restricted to the positive styles, not an overall successful verdict.
